description: LunarHaul vehicle and site catalogue: the single source of every vehicle number on screen and of the real dimensions the 3D models are built from. Every number is a quantity {value, unit, flag, source}. The engine's own constants (rover capacity, speed and night operation; lander payloads and descent constants) are mirrored here and checked equal by tests/test_catalog.py; the engine does not read this file. Loader: lunarsim/catalog.py. Schema: lunarsim/schemas/catalog-v1.schema.json. Written 22 Oct 2026 (B-30).

flags.Spec: a published specification or design value (URL in source)
flags.Measured: measured in flight or test (URL in source)
flags.Modelled: derived by our model or a stated calculation from sourced values
flags.Assumed: our assumption where nothing is published; the reasoning is in source

entries.name: CLPS-class lander (2 t at the gate)
entries.representative_note: Nova-C's published shape and size. The descent constants are the engine's SPLICE 2 t reference lander, not Nova-C's own (Nova-C is lighter). Alternative look: griffin. The leg span is not published (Assumed).

height_m.source: Nova-C height 3.938 m (the infobox says 3 m): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intuitive_Machines_Nova-C

diameter_m.source: Nova-C body 1.6 m (NASA NDL paper; Wikipedia gives 2 m): https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20250007036/downloads/aasimndl.pdf

leg_span_m.source: Nova-C's leg span is not published; drawn at the Apollo LM's ratio of footprint to body width, 9.4 m with landing gear extended / 4.22 m without = 2.23 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_Lunar_Module), x 1.6 m body

capacity_kg.source: upper bound of the engine's 100-500 kg payload per CLPS landing (lunarsim/scenario.py LANDER_TYPES); CLPS task orders deliver 0.07-0.475 t: https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/iparch10-wp-logistics-mobility-cargo.pdf

max_item_kg.source: largest single item on a CLPS landing (lunarsim/scenario.py LANDER_TYPES)

m_gate_kg.source: SPLICE robotic reference lander, 2,000 kg with a 5,000 N motor: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20200002415/downloads/20200002415.pdf [mirrors lunarsim/lander/classes.py]

prop_gate_kg.source: 15 % of gate mass; Assumed (terminal descent from the gate needs ~100 kg at Isp 311) [mirrors lunarsim/lander/classes.py]

t_min_n.source: 20 % throttle floor; Assumed (no CLPS throttle range published; Apollo DPS throttled to 10 %: https://www.lpi.usra.edu/lunar/documents/Bennett_NASA-TM-X-58040.pdf) [mirrors lunarsim/lander/classes.py]

isp_s.source: Apollo DPS full-thrust Isp 311 s used as a stand-in for a storable CLPS engine: https://www.lpi.usra.edu/lunar/documents/Bennett_NASA-TM-X-58040.pdf [mirrors lunarsim/lander/classes.py]

entries.propellant: LOX/LCH4 (Nova-C VR900; the descent model's 311 s Isp is the Apollo DPS stand-in)
entries.notes: Nova-C's ~1.9 t wet mass (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intuitive_Machines_Nova-C) matches the 2 t gate class. The descent model's 311 s Isp is a storable-propellant stand-in (Apollo DPS), so plume_class 'methalox' sets the look, not the physics.

entries.name: Blue Moon MK1-class lander (9 t at the gate)
entries.representative_note: Height and diameter are published; the landing legs are not (no source found), so the legs are a labelled representative shape. First flight (Pathfinder) NET Q1 2027.

leg_count.source: legs unpublished; four legs as on Apollo LM and Griffin

leg_span_m.source: MK1's leg span is not published; drawn at the Apollo LM's ratio of footprint to body width, 9.4 m with landing gear extended / 4.22 m without = 2.23 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_Lunar_Module), x 3.08 m body

capacity_kg.source: MK1 payload 3,000 kg to the surface: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Moon_(spacecraft) (engine: 2-3 t per landing)

max_item_kg.source: largest single item on an MK1 landing (lunarsim/scenario.py LANDER_TYPES); no published value

m_gate_kg.source: Blue Moon MK1 dry mass unpublished (21,350 kg fuelled, 3,000 kg payload); ~9,000 kg at the gate is Assumed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Moon_(spacecraft); a derived bound puts MK1's landed mass at 5.1-11.5 t, which one BE-7 can hover in every case (verification_round_1.md item 3) [mirrors lunarsim/lander/classes.py]

prop_gate_kg.source: Assumed in lunarsim/lander/classes.py (MK1); no published value [mirrors lunarsim/lander/classes.py]

t_max_n.source: BE-7 44 kN maximum, the one figure all sources agree on: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Moon_(spacecraft); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BE-7 [mirrors lunarsim/lander/classes.py]

t_min_n.source: BE-7 'throttling down to 2,000 lbf' (8.9 kN, 20 %): Blue Origin news release, 4 Dec 2020, https://www.blueorigin.com/news/be7-engine-testing (agrees with the 20-100 % in the BE-7 infobox; the 1,000 lbf figure has no source and is dropped; research_notes/.../verification_round_1.md item 3) [mirrors lunarsim/lander/classes.py]

isp_s.source: BE-7 vacuum Isp 460 s is uncited and ~453 s is an estimate; 440 s Assumed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BE-7 [mirrors lunarsim/lander/classes.py]

entries.notes: Hydrolox plume is nearly invisible (hydrogen flames in daylight: https://spinoff.nasa.gov/node/10136).

leg_span_m.source: HLS's leg span is not published; drawn at the Apollo LM's ratio of footprint to body width, 9.4 m with landing gear extended / 4.22 m without = 2.23 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_Lunar_Module), x 9 m body

capacity_kg.source: upper bound of the engine's 12-30 t per landing (lunarsim/scenario.py LANDER_TYPES); NASA quotes 12-15 t for the HLS cargo variants: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20250008728/downloads/25%2008%2026%20IAC_Creech%20BP-1.pdf

max_item_kg.source: the upper end of NASA's 12-15 t cargo-variant figure: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20250008728/downloads/25%2008%2026%20IAC_Creech%20BP-1.pdf

m_gate_kg.source: Parametric 60 t cargo lander (Starship HLS / Blue Moon MK2 cargo class; dry masses unpublished, cargo 12-15 t per NASA IAC 2025): reports/Lunar landing and rover autonomy logistics.md [mirrors lunarsim/lander/classes.py]

prop_gate_kg.source: Assumed in lunarsim/lander/classes.py (LARGE); no published value [mirrors lunarsim/lander/classes.py]

t_max_n.source: hover T/W 1.5 at the gate mass (Modelled) [mirrors lunarsim/lander/classes.py]

entries.propellant: LCH4/LOX (Raptor; GOX/GCH4 mid-body landing thrusters near the surface)
entries.notes: Reported to land on mid-body GOX/GCH4 thrusters within ~100 m of the surface: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starship_HLS

entries.name: LTV-class rover (1.5 t cargo)
entries.representative_note: CLV-1's final look is unpublished; FLEX's deployed envelope is used.

wheel_d_m.source: FLEX wheels 'an exceptional diameter of 930 mm' (Venturi, June 2023): https://www.venturi.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/PR_19_06_2023.pdf

wheelbase_m.source: not published; 70 % of the 4 m deployed length

track_m.source: not published; 2.3 m width less one wheel width (~0.3 m)

deck_height_m.source: not published and variable ('can raise and lower the chassis ground clearance', FLEX Payload Interface Guide v2.0: https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/mathews.pdf); 0.93 m wheel plus chassis

capacity_kg.source: 1,500 kg, within NASA's LTV capability of 800 kg at full and 1,600 kg at reduced performance: https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/iparch10-wp-logistics-mobility-cargo.pdf [the engine's value; see lunarsim/entities.py and the paper's Table 3]

speed_kmh.source: 10 km/h design speed modelled as a 6 km/h autonomous average; CLV-1 '>6 mph on level terrain': https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-provides-update-on-moon-base-rovers-landers-missions/ [the engine's value; see lunarsim/entities.py and the paper's Table 3]

night_ops.source: survives the night (requirement 85-125 h of darkness) but does not drive in it; the engine parks it [the engine's value; see lunarsim/entities.py and the paper's Table 3]

entries.notes: FLEX payload guide (2022 prototype): top-deck payload envelope 1.5 x 0.75 x 2.5 m, standard underslung containers 1.5 x 1.0/1.5/2.0 x 1.0 m, robotic arm >25 kg within 2 m: https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/mathews.pdf

entries.name: Heavy hauler (10 t cargo, works at night; concept)
entries.representative_note: No flown or built counterpart: NASA lists >1,600 kg relocation as a capability that does not exist. Drawn as a generic low flat-bed on six wheels with a pallet interface, radiators and headlights, no solar mast; labelled 'concept'. Every dimension is Assumed.

length_m.source: deck long enough for a 6 m cargo element lying flat; illustrative

width_m.source: about 1.5x ATHLETE gen-1's 2.75 m width for a 10 t payload; illustrative

height_m.source: standing height a little above ATHLETE gen-1's ~2 m; illustrative

wheel_count.source: six wheel-on-leg limbs, as on ATHLETE: https://robotics.jpl.nasa.gov/how-we-do-it/systems/the-athlete-rover/

wheel_d_m.source: about twice the LRV's 0.818 m wheel, for a ~4 kN wheel load ((10 t + 4 t) x 1.62 m/s^2 / 6); illustrative, not a design

track_m.source: 4 m width less one wheel width; illustrative

deck_height_m.source: walking legs can raise it; ATHLETE was designed to offload from a 3.2 m lander deck: https://www-robotics.jpl.nasa.gov/media/documents/Heverly_2010_AMS_Tri-ATHLETE.pdf

mass_kg.source: ~4 t landed, the figure behind the engine's $600M unit cost (lunarsim/entities.py)

capacity_kg.source: proxy for the 'high capacity mobility' NASA lists as missing above 1,600 kg: https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/iparch10-wp-logistics-mobility-cargo.pdf [the engine's value; see lunarsim/entities.py and the paper's Table 3]

speed_kmh.source: slower than the LTV with a 10 t load [the engine's value; see lunarsim/entities.py and the paper's Table 3]

night_ops.source: built to work through the lunar night (the reason it exists in the model) [the engine's value; see lunarsim/entities.py and the paper's Table 3]

entries.name: Small utility rover (0.3 t cargo)
entries.representative_note: VIPER's published geometry at true scale. Capacity and speed are the engine's MICRO class, modelled on the Lunar Outpost HL-MAPP (250 kg rover, 200 kg payload), not VIPER.

length_m.source: VIPER 1.7 x 1.7 x 2.5 m: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20240013903/downloads/LSIC_2024-Tech%20Infusion_Panel-VIPER_Mob-HW.pdf (NASA's mission page says 1.5 m: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/viper/rover-and-instruments)

width_m.source: VIPER 1.7 x 1.7 x 2.5 m: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20240013903/downloads/LSIC_2024-Tech%20Infusion_Panel-VIPER_Mob-HW.pdf (NASA's mission page says 1.5 m: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/viper/rover-and-instruments)

height_m.source: VIPER 1.7 x 1.7 x 2.5 m (to the mast top): https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20240013903/downloads/LSIC_2024-Tech%20Infusion_Panel-VIPER_Mob-HW.pdf

capacity_kg.source: HL-MAPP class carries 200 kg: https://lunaroutpost.com/rovers; modelled 300 kg [the engine's value; see lunarsim/entities.py and the paper's Table 3]

speed_kmh.source: HL-MAPP up to 3 m/s: https://lunaroutpost.com/rovers; modelled 3 km/h average [the engine's value; see lunarsim/entities.py and the paper's Table 3]

night_ops.source: parks at night [the engine's value; see lunarsim/entities.py and the paper's Table 3]

entries.name: Surface habitat module (NASA Common Habitat class)
entries.representative_note: A NASA design concept (SLS-tank-derived) for Moon and Mars base camps; no surface habitat has a published final shape.

diameter_m.source: '8.4 meters in diameter and 15.6 meters in length' (Howard et al., ASCEND 2023): https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20220010430

length_m.source: '8.4 meters in diameter and 15.6 meters in length': https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20220010430 (a 2022 AIAA paper gives 15 m)

mass_kg.source: 'may mass as much as 90-tons when initially deployed', crew of eight: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20220010430

entries.notes: Far heavier than any item the engine moves (largest element 15 t): scenery, landed in place.

entries.name: Landing pad with ejecta berm

reference_vehicle.name: Metzger & Autry 2022 pad; NASA KSC Lunar Innovation Park berm

entries.representative_note: Published design dimensions; the berm was sized by NASA KSC for CLPS-class landers.

diameter_m.source: Artemis-era two-zone pad of 27 m radius (Metzger & Autry 2022): https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.00378. Default for every class; the Artemis HLS-class pad requirement is 100-200 m (200 m, being negotiated to 100 m: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20220000334/downloads/In%20situ%20Lunar%20Launch%20and%20Landing%20Pad%20Construction%20with%20Regolith%20and%20Thermoset%20Polymers%20ASCE%20Earth%20and%20Space%202022%20Paper%20SUBMITTED.pdf), to revisit when a LARGE lander lands on it (F-36)

berm_height_m.source: 2.5 m berm (lander height with VSAT stowed), NASA KSC Lunar Innovation Park: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20260002816/downloads/329%20-%20Site%20Plan%20and%20Bulk%20Presentation.pdf

berm_radius_m.source: berm centreline = 27 m pad radius + KSC's 8 m standoff from the berm face + half the 4.9 m base (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20260002816/downloads/329%20-%20Site%20Plan%20and%20Bulk%20Presentation.pdf)

entries.notes: KSC's reusable pad: 20 m compacted foundation, 15 m durable surface, two 9 m accessways at 5 deg: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20260002816/downloads/329%20-%20Site%20Plan%20and%20Bulk%20Presentation.pdf. No berm has been designed for 15-100 t landers (KSC's outer berm handles a 6 deg ejecta angle).

entries.name: Vertical solar array tower (VSAT class)
entries.representative_note: Mast height and power are NASA's; the array shape differs between the funded designs and its width is not published for the 10 kW class.

height_m.source: 'deploy up to 32 feet high' (NASA: https://www.nasa.gov/technology/nasa-industry-to-mature-vertical-solar-array-technologies-for-lunar-surface/); '~10 kWe class array ... on a >10 m tower' (BEACON, Oleson et al. 2025: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20240015887/downloads/BEACON%20Exec%20Summary.pdf)

array_height_m.source: upper 70 % of the 10 m mast, so the array clears local terrain by 3 m

array_width_m.source: area for 10 kW at the areal power of Astrobotic's VSAT-XL (50 kW from 20 m x 12.5 m = 200 W/m^2: https://www.astrobotic.com/astrobotic-developing-xl-solar-array-tech-for-lunar-power-infrastructure/; https://www.astrobotic.com/astrobotic-awarded-lunar-power-study-with-vsat-xl/) = 50 m^2, over a 7 m array height

entries.notes: Taller designs: Lockheed Martin up to 65 ft (https://www.lockheedmartin.com/en-us/news/features/2025/powering-the-moon--vertical-solar-arrays-charge-the-way-.html); Astrobotic VSAT-XL 34 m tall x 12.5 m wide, 50 kW (https://www.astrobotic.com/astrobotic-awarded-lunar-power-study-with-vsat-xl/).

entries.notes: Honeybee's LUNARSABER is proposed at over 100 m: https://www.blueorigin.com/news/honeybee-robotics-to-develop-lunarsaber-for-darpas-luna-10-program
